subject: Tilted demo windows: NYC customer + Berlin engineers — proposed split-host approach
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@novamed.com>
Cc: Mark Davis <mark.davis@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Tilted demo windows: NYC customer + Berlin engineers — proposed split-host approach

Hi Patricia / Mark —

Thanks again for your time last week. We’re excited to demo the Redwood Inference flow for NovaMed. I flagged availability with our Berlin engineering team and ran into a DST timing wrinkle (EU and US fall-back dates are off by a week this year), so I want to propose a slightly different approach that avoids everyone joining at 02:00 local.

Quick proposals:
- Option A (single session): 08:00 CET / 02:00 EDT on Tue 3 Nov — less than ideal for NovaMed ops, I know.
- Option B (split-hosted session): 18:00 EDT / 00:00 CET — Redwood EU leads the technical deep-dive for the first 30 mins, NovaMed joins the last 30 mins for Q&A; we record the whole run and provide a short handoff recording for the folks who can’t attend live.
- Option C (staggered 2-window demo): 14:00 EDT / 20:00 CET — two short 30-min windows covering product overview + engineering deep-dive in separate slots (allows some overlap for live Q&A).

I attached a draft agenda and a calendar with the three timestamps. Please tell me which one fits your team, or propose an alternate — happy to adapt. If we go with the split-host Option B we’ll make sure a recording and time-stamped notes are shared immediately after.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tilted demo windows: NYC customer + Berlin engineers — proposed split-host approach

Ben —

Thanks for laying out options and for the heads-up on DST. Our ops team is not keen on 02:00 EDT; Option A is a non-starter. Option C looks promising, though we have two engineers who can only join early in the morning (before 10am ET). Option B might work if the recorded segment captures the full engineering walkthrough and the last 15–20 minutes are live for questions.

Two asks: can you confirm the recording will include the console/network latency graphs and the sample prompt suite? Also, do you have a brief checklist of what NovaMed should prepare (example prompts, sample files) so our engineers are ready?

—Patricia

Subject: Fwd: Tilted demo windows — need EU-side confirmation and recording scope

Laura / Vivek —

Looping you in — NovaMed prefers not to do a 02:00 ET live session. Patricia is open to a split-host Option B (Redwood EU runs the heavy engineering walkthrough, then NovaMed joins for the last 20–30 mins). They need the recording to include console views, latency/throughput graphs, and the prompt suite. Can you confirm we can:
1) Record the session (video + shared-screen) and produce a 7–10 min highlight clip + time-stamped notes.
2) Include the infra/latency dashboards during the walk-through.
3) Run the sample prompt set listed in the agenda so we have concrete examples for them.

If that’s doable, please propose two concrete local times for Berlin-based leads (we want one that’s late evening CET and one that’s late afternoon CET) so I can push those back to Patricia with exact ET equivalents.

Thanks —
Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:45:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tilted demo windows — need EU-side confirmation and recording scope

Ben / Vivek —

We can absolutely run Option B and capture everything Patricia requested. Confirming we will:
- Record the full session (mp4) and produce a 7–10 min highlight clip plus a time-stamped markdown notes file.
- Share the Performance dashboard (token latency, p50/p95, throughput) and run the sample prompt suite from the agenda.
- Provide the raw recording and highlight clip within 24 hours; time-stamped notes within 48 hours.

Two Berlin-friendly slots (local CET/CEST labels):
- Slot 1: Tue 9 Nov 20:30 CET (14:30 EST / 11:30 PST) — late evening Berlin, mid-afternoon New York. Overlap: 30 mins for live Q&A.
- Slot 2: Wed 10 Nov 18:00 CET (12:00 EST / 09:00 PST) — earlier evening Berlin; middle-of-day NY; longer overlap if needed.

Note on DST: our calendar shows EU switches back on Sun 1 Nov (CEST -> CET) while US switches on Sun 8 Nov this year, so the one-week mismatch you mentioned may still affect early-Nov slots. I’ve verified Slot 1 and Slot 2 conversions are correct for the current DST offsets and are stable across the next two weeks.

If either of those work, we’ll set up the runbook and assign a dedicated recording + ops owner.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Staff Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — glad Option B is acceptable. Based on Laura’s availability we recommend Slot 1: Tue 9 Nov 20:30 CET which is 14:30 EDT for NovaMed—this gives a 30–45 minute live overlap and a full recording we’ll deliver the next day.

Prep checklist for NovaMed (short):
- Provide 3–5 representative prompts/scenarios (anonymized) to run in the demo.
- A single example dataset (CSV) if you want us to show embedding/recall flow.
- Names of the 1–2 engineers who will attend (we’ll tag Q&A time to them).
- Any compliance questions up-front (SOC2/audit logs) so we can surface the right console screens.

I’ll send a tentative calendar invite for Tue 9 Nov 14:30 EDT / 20:30 CET; if that doesn’t work we’ll pivot to Wed 10 Nov 12:00 EDT / 18:00 CET.

Cheers,
Ben
